consumer: The frontend's per-monster 'has noticed the avatar' flag, which asks whether the engine considers the avatar a detected/tracked target of each monster.
scope: Each in-window monster's engine-computed awareness/tracking state toward the avatar (whether the monster sees or is hunting the player), not merely its presence or position.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_entities (monsters window) — it loops g->all_monsters(), filters by in_export_window, and writes index/type_id/pos/hp/hp_max/hallucination, but reads no monster awareness/sees-player/anger/target field at all.
divergence: A monster sits inside the export window but is asleep and has not detected the avatar (monster::sees(player)==false / no player target): the surface lists it with full HP and position, so a frontend deriving 'noticed' from mere presence flags it as having noticed when the engine predicate says it has not.
